chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Qāsim ibn al-Ṣayqal, who said:

I wrote to him: May I be made your ransom, did Amīr al-Muʾminīn, may the prayers of Allah be upon him, perform ghusl when he washed the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, at the time of his death? So he answered him: “The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, is pure and purified, but Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام did perform it, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) has proceeded accordingly.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established prophetic tradition or normative practice

ai.seo_question: Did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام perform ghusl after washing the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith states that although the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was inherently pure and purified, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام nevertheless performed ghusl after washing him. It indicates that this act became an established sunnah (prophetic tradition) in relation to washing the deceased.
